questions.prompt: Which two properties define a Redis Set?

options.text: Ordered by score, members are unique

questions.explanation: A Set is an unordered collection of unique members; adding a duplicate has no effect. (Ordering by score describes a Sorted Set.)

questions.prompt: Which command returns the members present in ALL of the given sets?
questions.explanation: SINTER computes the intersection (members in every set). SUNION is the union, SDIFF is the difference.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Set commands are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: SADD returns the number of newly added members
SINTERCARD returns the size of an intersection without materializing it
SISMEMBER tests whether a member is in the set
SMEMBERS is a paginated, cheap way to read huge sets

questions.explanation: SADD counts new members, SINTERCARD gives just the intersection size, and SISMEMBER tests membership. SMEMBERS is O(N) and unpaginated — use SSCAN for large sets.

questions.prompt: You want to store the result of a set intersection to reuse it later. Which command helps?
questions.explanation: SINTERSTORE writes the intersection into a destination key so you can reuse it, rather than recomputing with SINTER each time.

questions.prompt: The command that returns the number of members in a set (its cardinality) is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: SCARD returns the member count of a set in O(1).

questions.prompt: Which is the best use case for a Set rather than a List?

options.text: A FIFO job queue where order matters
The distinct tags on an article, where uniqueness matters and order does not
The last 100 log lines in order

questions.explanation: Sets shine when you need uniqueness and membership tests without ordering — like tags. Queues want a List; rankings want a Sorted Set.
